headline: Consent is permission freely given—asking before acting and respecting whatever answer comes
universal_truth: People have autonomy over themselves; respecting others' no is as important as seeking their yes
fun_facts: Consent applies to much more than physical touch—time, attention, space, and information all require consent
Clear consent improves relationships by establishing mutual respect and trust
Healthy consent is enthusiastic, informed, and freely revocable at any time
discussion_questions: Where do you assume permission instead of asking?
How do you respond when someone says no to you?
What's the difference between reluctant compliance and genuine consent?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: May I? This simple question recognizes that others have autonomy—you don't have the right to act on them without permission. Consent is asking before acting, and respecting whatever answer comes. Even when it's no.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Consent seems simple but is often overlooked or coerced. What makes consent real versus performed?

options.text: Genuine consent is freely given, informed, and revocable—without pressure, with understanding, and with the real option to say no or change your mind; anything less isn't true consent
options.response: Yes. Consent under pressure isn't consent. Consent without information isn't consent. Consent that can't be withdrawn isn't consent. Real consent is free, informed, and ongoing.
Saying yes is necessary, but the conditions matter—was it free, informed, and revocable?

q1.title: Respecting No
q1.script: How you handle 'no' reveals your respect for consent. If you push, persuade, or punish refusal, you're not actually seeking consent—you're seeking compliance. Respect means accepting the answer.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Respecting No"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Broad Application
q2.script: Consent applies beyond the physical: borrowing someone's time, sharing their information, entering their space. Many boundary violations happen because people assume permission instead of asking.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Consent Culture
q3.script: Building consent as habit improves all relationships. Ask instead of assume. Respect refusal. Make it safe to say no. This creates trust, not awkwardness.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: People have autonomy over themselves. Respecting others' no is as important as seeking their yes. Ask and accept the answer.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 320! Tomorrow, we'll explore where you end and others begin—boundaries. Until then, notice where you assume permission.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Consent Check - Where Do You Assume Permission?
growTrack.activity: Where do you act without asking—with others' time, space, information, attention? Practice asking permission in one area you usually assume. Notice how you handle 'no' when it comes.
